scenario: AITA for making a Facebook post about someone without telling them? | My (22F) best friend (21M) recently went on a 3 month long trip to India to do volunteer work. He helped to build a water pipeline and taught kids in a local school about hygiene and sanitation. He also paid for the whole trip himself, costing over $3000. He is a pretty shy and quiet guy, so he didn’t tell many people about it before he left and I doubt he was going to when he got back if I didn’t do this. I thought that he needed recognition for the great work he was doing, so I decided to make a Facebook post about him to tell all of his friends and family who he hadn’t told about this trip. I did this while he was away, about a week before he got home. Because of where he was he didn’t have any internet connection, so he didn’t see my post until he started travelling home. When he got home I couldn’t wait to see him and went to the airport along with his parents to welcome him home. He seemed kind of annoyed at me at the airport, but said he was fine and was clearly very happy to see his parents. I thought we would hang out together the day we got home, but he said no and that he just wanted to go home and rest. I decided to text him that evening to ask again what was wrong. He told me he was pissed off at me for the Facebook post. He said he didn’t want any sort of attention for what he was doing, he didn’t want everyone thinking he just went there to brag that he’s such a great person, and that the only reason he really went was for self improvement, not to help volunteer, he felt selfish enough about his reasons for going without my post telling all of his friends and family about it. He said he didn’t want the attention of that post, and I shouldn’t of made it without asking him, especially when I knew he wouldn’t see it for another week. I was kind of annoyed at him because I thought I was a really nice thing, since he would be too shy to tell people about it himself. The post was so positive about him, I didn’t say anything bad. AITA for making that post?

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether I did the right thing by making that Facebook post about my best friend's trip to India. Let me start by laying out the situation as I understand it. My best friend, who's 21, went on a three-month trip to India to do volunteer work. He helped build a water pipeline and taught kids in a local school about hygiene and sanitation. That's pretty impressive, right? And he even paid for the entire trip himself, which cost over $3000. Now, he's a pretty shy and quiet guy, so he didn't tell many people about the trip before he left. I'm not sure if he was planning to tell anyone when he got back either. I thought he needed recognition for the great work he did, so I decided to make a Facebook post about him to let all his friends and family know about the trip. I did this while he was away, about a week before he got home. Because of where he was, he didn't have any internet connection, so he didn't see my post until he started traveling home. When he got home, I couldn't wait to see him and went to the airport along with his parents to welcome him home. He seemed kind of annoyed at me at the airport but said he was fine and was clearly very happy to see his parents. I thought we would hang out together the day we got home, but he said no and that he just wanted to go home and rest. I decided to text him that evening to ask again what was wrong. He told me he was pissed off at me for the Facebook post. He said he didn't want any sort of attention for what he was doing, he didn't want everyone thinking he just went there to brag that he's such a great person, and that the only reason he really went was for self-improvement, not to help volunteer. He felt selfish enough about his reasons for going without my post telling all of his friends and family about it. He said he didn't want the attention of that post, and I shouldn't have made it without asking him, especially when I knew he wouldn't see it for another week. I was kind of annoyed at him because I thought I was doing a really nice thing, since he would be too shy to tell people about it himself. The post was so positive about him; I didn't say anything bad. So, was I AITA (Against My Better Judgment) for making that post? Alright, so to figure this out, I need to consider a few things. First, I need to understand what AITA means. From what I know, AITA stands for "Am I the Asshole?" It's a way to evaluate whether someone's actions were inappropriate or hurtful, even if they didn't intend to be. So, in this case, I need to determine if making the Facebook post without my friend's consent was AITA. Let me break it down: 1. **Intentions**: My intention was to recognize my friend for the good work he did. I thought it was a nice thing to do because he's shy and wouldn't tell people himself. I wanted to highlight his positive actions and make sure others knew about his efforts. 2. **Friend's Feelings**: My friend, however, felt the opposite. He didn't want any attention for his trip. He went for self-improvement, not to seek recognition or help others. He felt that my post made it seem like he was bragging or seeking attention, which went against his reasons for going. 3. **Communication**: I didn't ask my friend before making the post. I assumed he would appreciate the recognition, but I didn't check in with him. He only found out about the post when he got home, and by then, it was already shared with his friends and family. 4. **Impact**: The post had an unintended negative impact on our relationship. My friend was upset and felt disrespected because I didn't consider his wishes before sharing something personal about him. 5. **Boundaries**: Making a post about someone else's personal experiences without their consent can be seen as overstepping boundaries. It's important to respect others' privacy and their desire for or against attention. 6. **Self-Reflection**: I need to reflect on why I thought it was a good idea to make the post. Was it to support my friend, or was it to share something impressive about him to others? Understanding my own motivations can help clarify whether my actions were appropriate. 7. **Alternative Actions**: What could I have done differently? Maybe I could have talked to my friend about his trip and asked him if he wanted to share it with others. If he didn't, I could have respected his wishes and not made the post. 8. **Consequences**: The consequences of my actions were that my friend felt upset and our relationship was strained. It's important to consider how our actions might affect others, especially when it comes to their privacy and feelings. 9. **Learning Opportunity**: This situation can be a learning opportunity for both of us. For me, it's about respecting others' boundaries and communication before sharing personal information. For my friend, it's about expressing his feelings clearly and trusting that I will respect his wishes in the future. 10. **Moving Forward**: How can we move past this? It might involve having an open conversation about our feelings, setting clear boundaries, and ensuring that both of us feel respected and heard in the future. After considering all these points, it seems like making the Facebook post without my friend's consent was AITA. While my intentions were good, I didn't respect his boundaries and his desire for privacy. It's important to communicate and get consent before sharing personal information about others, especially when it involves their choices and feelings.
